name: Apurímac
summary_text: No documented sub-national signal for Apurímac: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds Apurímac is the national frame: a congressional bill package (6506/8457, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no regional deviation documented either way.

sources.title: Congreso aprueba norma que atenta contra el derecho de las personas trans a usar baños públicos - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae national news report (20 Feb 2025): the congressional committee on women and family approved unanimously the report backing bills 6506 and 8457 (lawmakers Montoya and Munante), which bar trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite their birth sex - with exceptions for custody, medical care and accompanying children under 12, elderly or disabled people - and require unambiguous facility signage; the opinion still needs full-chamber approval. An LGBTI activist quoted calls the measure discriminatory.

sources.title: Discriminación legalizada: sobre la prohibición del Congreso a personas trans para acceder a baños públicos - IDEHPUCP
sources.claim_summary: IDEHPUCP (human-rights institute, Pontifical Catholic University of Peru) bulletin: academic critique of the congressional bathroom ban - argues the law implicitly brands trans people as a sexual risk to minors in facilities, citing a lawmaker's ridicule of trans bathroom use; part of the institute's coverage of legalised discrimination (incl. INDECOPI discrimination rulings).

sources.title: Perú: aumentaron los crímenes de odio y las mujeres trans son las más afectadas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Presentes news report (22 Jul 2024) on the UPCH Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI annual report: 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023, with trans women the most affected group and hate crimes rising; includes testimony on the February 2023 murder of a trans woman kidnapped from downtown Lima and shot dead by a criminal gang in Carabayllo.
